title: Positive tangent weights turn an equivariant local inverse into a global inverse
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth connected affine $F$-schemes of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Give each a $\mathbf G_m$-action [def-sc-gm-ga], meaning an $F$-morphism $\mathbf G_m\times_F X\to X$ (respectively with $Y$) satisfying the action identity and associativity. Let $x\in X(F)$ and $y\in Y(F)$ be fixed points, and let $f:X\to Y$ be an $F$-morphism with $f(x)=y$ and $f(tz)=t f(z)$ as an identity of scheme morphisms. Put $T_xX=\operatorname{Hom}_F(\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2,F)$ and define $T_yY$ likewise; the differential $d f_x:T_xX\to T_yY$ is the dual of pullback on these cotangent spaces. Assume $d f_x$ is an isomorphism and that, for the differentiated action, $T_xX$ is a direct sum of subspaces on which $t$ acts by $t^n$ with integers $n>0$. Weights here mean characters of $\mathbf G_m$, not differentials of characters. Then $f$ is an isomorphism of $F$-schemes. The zero tangent space is allowed, with an empty set of weights, and no restriction on $\operatorname{char}F$ is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 13.42 and its proof, printed p.270, using Theorem 13.41, pp.269--270; the smooth-variety differential criterion for etaleness is stated immediately before Lemma 13.35, p.267. The torus is specialized to G_m and both varieties are assumed smooth.

proof.text: Put $C_Y=\mathfrak m_y/\mathfrak m_y^2$ and $C_X=\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2$. Pullback induces $c:C_Y\to C_X$ and its dual is $df_x$. These spaces are finite-dimensional (apply [lem-sfb-fixed-point-homogeneous-cotangent-lifts] to each). Thus $c$ is invertible: dualize the inverse of $df_x$ and use the evaluation identifications with the double duals. Differentiating the given equivariance identity gives $df_x\,d(t)_x=d(t)_y\,df_x$. Hence $T_yY$ has precisely the positive character weights of $T_xX$, in every characteristic.

source.place: Corollary 13.42, first sentence of proof, p.270; Lemma 13.36 for finite cotangent bases.

proof.text: Choose homogeneous $b_1,\ldots,b_d\in\mathfrak m_y$ whose classes form a basis, by [lem-sfb-fixed-point-homogeneous-cotangent-lifts]. Set $a_i=f^*b_i\in\mathfrak m_x$. Their classes are $c(\overline b_i)$ and form a basis since $c$ is invertible. Equivariance gives $a_i(tu)=b_i(f(tu))=b_i(tf(u))=t^{n_i}a_i(u)$ as scheme identities. Thus these are homogeneous lifts on $X$ as well. Apply [lem-sfb-positive-weight-luna-coordinates] first to $(Y,y,b_i)$ and then to $(X,x,a_i)$. Smoothness, connectedness, affineness and finite type are hypotheses for both schemes; positivity for $Y$ is step 1. The coordinate maps $\lambda_Y:Y\to\mathbf A_F^d$ and $\lambda_X:X\to\mathbf A_F^d$ are isomorphisms.

source.place: Corollary 13.42, commutative diagram and concluding sentence, p.270; Theorem 13.41.

proof.text: The two homomorphisms $F[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ defining $\lambda_Y\circ f$ and $\lambda_X$ send every $T_i$ to $f^*b_i=a_i$. They are equal by the polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], so contravariant functoriality and uniqueness for affine spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum] give $\lambda_Y\circ f=\lambda_X$. Consequently $f=\lambda_Y^{-1}\circ\lambda_X$; its two-sided inverse is $\lambda_X^{-1}\circ\lambda_Y$. For $d=0$ the same calculation uses the empty polynomial ring $F$. This proves the asserted scheme isomorphism.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q68-ff0a12b5c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all of the item's mathematics and passed it without changes. Source checked: Milne iAG pp.267-270 (the Luna-map paragraph, 13.35-13.42). The item is Milne 13.42 for T=G_m with X and Y smooth; its statement is unchanged and every hypothesis matches the source. Step 1 shows c=(df_x)^dual is invertible using finite-dimensionality from the lifts node, and the chain rule on f∘a_t=a_t∘f carries the positive character weights over to T_yY. Step 2 pulls back homogeneous target lifts b_i, giving a_i=f^*b_i: these lie in m_x, form a basis via c, and are homogeneous as a scheme identity. It then applies the Luna-coordinates node to (Y,y,b) and (X,x,a), and every hypothesis is available for both. Step 3 is elementary: polynomial uniqueness and the Spec bijection give λ_Y∘f=λ_X, so f=λ_Y^{-1}λ_X. New node lem-sfb-fixed-point-homogeneous-cotangent-lifts (13.36 for G_m) is true without smoothness or characteristic restrictions: the action is a Z-grading, m is graded because z is fixed, and m/m^2 is finite-dimensional. I tested it on d=0, on F[e]/(e^2) with any weight, and on the cusp with weights (2,3). New node lem-sfb-positive-weight-luna-coordinates (13.41 for G_m) is true. Smooth and connected makes Z integral, positive tangent weights force n_i>0, and Krull intersection then gives an N-grading with A_0=F; graded Nakayama makes λ a closed immersion, and comparing dimensions makes it an isomorphism. I tested it on d=0, on A^1 with weight 1, and on (u,v+u^2) with weights (1,2); with weight 0 the conclusion fails, and the positivity hypothesis excludes that case. Neither new node duplicates lem-sfb-positive-graded-regular-polynomial, which assumes the N-grading the Luna node derives, or the luna-borel/projective-attracting nodes. The Luna node is the Y=A^d special case, which is the source's own 13.41-then-13.42 order, not a restatement of the item. B1-B7 forms, created.item and proof_deps are correct. No SGA source, no tool_uses, and the item's citers are unaffected.
